After walking back down the hallway, he and Jetta come through the door; he leaves the bloodstained ax on a table. Jetta goes into the living room, and Desmond brings whisky and glasses. He pours drinks for them and drinks his quickly, while Jetta asks what happened. Desmond says it concerned a kid who fought with Pop, and they share a joke and laugh. Desmond says he needs sleep; Jetta says she wanted to talk, but he puts it off until morning and offers her the bed that night. Jetta decides to bathe first. Desmond gets a blanket from the linen closet as Jetta walks slowly into the bathroom.

plotBeats: Desmond enters his apartment, turns on the kitchen lights, pulls a .45-caliber handgun from behind his back, and places it on the counter.
He opens a drawer of tools and takes a roofing ax.
He walks back down the hallway to the door; minutes later, Desmond and Jetta enter, and he throws the bloodstained ax onto a table.
Jetta goes to the living room while Desmond gets glasses and a bottle of Jack Daniels from the kitchen and joins her.
Seeing Jetta exhausted and with blood on her shirt, Desmond pours whisky for both and gives her a glass.
Desmond drinks his glass and then gulps from the bottle; he thanks Jetta.
Jetta asks what happened, and Desmond says it involved a kid who fought with Pop, criticizing the young man and modern hip-hop.
Jetta jokes, “How about some hard core,” and they both laugh.
Desmond says he is finished for the night and needs sleep; Jetta says she wanted to talk.
Desmond says they can talk in the morning, offers her the bed tonight, and says she will have the couch after that.
Jetta says she will take a bath before bed; Desmond tells her to go ahead.
Desmond stumbles to the linen closet and takes a blanket as Jetta slowly walks to the bathroom to bathe.

speaking.emotional_state: exhausted and matter-of-fact, with brief amusement
speaking.goal: Explain the bloody incident involving a kid and Pop, then end the conversation and get some sleep.
speaking.name: Desmond

speaking.emotional_state: exhausted but lightly joking, then intent on talking
speaking.goal: Find out what happened and raise something she wants to discuss.
speaking.name: Jetta

scene_01M4KD5YMZK3P49RMRPK71HHRW.title: A Reason to Live
scene_01M4KD5YMZK3P49RMRPK71HHRW.summary: Fifth watches the sunrise from the roof, then goes inside and takes a bath while Madison wakes and joins him in the bathroom. She notices his bandaged wrists and questions him about his suicide attempts and his bleak view of life. They argue about what makes life valuable, his wealth and charitable giving, and whether he has reasons to live. A leak from the bathroom prompts Sidney downstairs to yell about damage to her prints, and Fifth insults her while Madison urges him to talk to her. Fifth explains his financial arrangements with Des and the limits he places on his suicide methods. Madison tries to encourage him, then reveals that their father was ill and says Fifth's thinking resembles his. Fifth submerges his head in the bath, and Madison leaves.

plotBeats: Fifth watches the sunrise from dangerously near the roof's edge, smiling, then moves away and goes inside.
Fifth gets orange juice from the fridge and heads to the bathroom, where he draws a bath; Madison wakes on the sofa and joins him.
Madison and Fifth exchange morning greetings and talk about sleep and the sunrise; Madison warns him to stay off the roof.
Madison notices the bandages on Fifth's wrists and questions him about harming himself; he says he has long wanted to end his life and sees little meaning in living.
Madison challenges Fifth's outlook and argues that wealth and outward advantages do not define what either of them wants; Fifth says the money he made was for their mother and means nothing to him.
Madison flushes the toilet, prompting Fifth to explain that water from it or the tub leaks downstairs; Sidney bangs and yells that the leak is ruining her prints, and Fifth insults her.
Madison urges Fifth to talk to Sidney; he says he has never met her and reacts dismissively.
Madison suggests making breakfast; Fifth says the fridge is empty and the gas is off, and he has no money on him.
Fifth explains that he gave most of his money to the poor, left the loft to Des, and depends on Des for food money with receipts required to discourage him from buying a gun.
Madison asks whether Fifth has tried using a gun; Fifth says there are methods he will not use and lists several ways he would not kill himself.

Madison says she does not believe he is serious; Fifth describes his long-standing despair, while Madison urges him to see the beauty and struggles in the world and remember his sister and best friend.
Fifth says he must find a reason to live for himself; Madison tells him their father was sick and says Fifth resembles him in his thinking.
Fifth gives Madison a dismissive look and dunks his head under the bathwater; Madison walks out of the bathroom.

speaking.goal: Understand and challenge Fifth's self-harm and despair, then urge him to speak with Sidney and find reasons to live.
speaking.name: Madison

speaking.goal: Explain his lack of purpose and resistance to living for others, and respond to Madison and the neighbor.
speaking.name: Fifth

speaking.goal: Get Fifth to repair the leaking pipe that is damaging her prints.
speaking.name: Sidney

scene_01M4KD5YMZW4MZQTGAGT5SB2P7.title: A Morning Interrupted
scene_01M4KD5YMZW4MZQTGAGT5SB2P7.summary: Desmond takes a phone call and prepares to leave for a meeting. Jetta appears, and they exchange flirtatious remarks before she asks to talk. He postpones the conversation, tells her there is cash in the coffee can, and leaves. Outside, he asks Jonesy to hose blood from the steps, suggesting kids played on the stoop, then drives off. Jetta watches him go and finds an old picture of herself and Desmond in his bedroom.

plotBeats: Desmond eats cereal by the window and answers a phone call, agreeing to meet at Knick's in fifteen minutes.
He gets dressed as Jetta emerges from the room; he compliments her appearance and she calls his remarks bullshit.
Jetta offers coffee; Desmond says he must leave for a meeting. Jetta says she thought they would talk, but he puts it off and asks about her plans.
Jetta says she needs to look for a job. Desmond tells her there is cash in the coffee can and leaves.
Desmond sees bloodstains on the steps and asks Jonesy to hose them down, saying some kids may have played on his stoop.
Jonesy agrees; Desmond crosses the street, sees there is no ticket, gets in his car, and drives away.
Jetta watches him leave, wanders through the apartment, and enters his neat bedroom.
She picks up a face-down picture frame and sees an old, happy picture of herself and Desmond, which she stares at.

speaking.emotional_state: casual, then rushed; conciliatory toward Jetta
speaking.goal: Take a call, attend his meeting, and postpone talking with Jetta while offering her cash.
speaking.name: Desmond

speaking.goal: Talk with Desmond and make plans to look for work.
speaking.name: Jetta

scene_01M4KD5YMZDFKT1MGZ53FWCQ78.title: Dressed to Go
scene_01M4KD5YMZDFKT1MGZ53FWCQ78.summary: Fifth gets dressed in a “We're Pregnant” T-shirt and Cub scout hat, then comes out wearing yellow sneakers while Madison urges him to hurry. They plan to go shopping, but Fifth says they are both broke; Madison points out that he is wealthy and asks about his credit cards and store accounts, which he says are gone or closed. Madison opts for Central Park. They leave the loft and encounter Jessie at the entrance, where Sidney and Fifth make eye contact and look back at each other.

plotBeats: Fifth gets dressed in his bedroom and enters a walk-in closet filled with suits, shoes, and T-shirts.
He puts on a “We're Pregnant” T-shirt, grabs a Cub scout hat, and searches for shoes while Madison asks if he is ready.
Fifth emerges wearing yellow sneakers; Madison looks him over and responds, “Whatever.”
Madison says they are going shopping; Fifth points out that they are both broke.
Madison says she is broke but Fifth is loaded, and asks about his credit cards and store accounts; Fifth says they are gone and all closed.
Madison decides they will go to Central Park instead.
Fifth and Madison leave, take the elevator to the ground floor, and encounter Jessie coming in at the door.
Sidney and Fifth make eye contact and both turn to look back at each other.

speaking.name: Madison

scene_01M4KD5YMZ5BVCAVJWNZ9WY867.title: Neighborly Advice
scene_01M4KD5YMZ5BVCAVJWNZ9WY867.summary: Fifth and Madison walk down a busy New York street. Madison asks whether Fifth knows a woman; he says he has never seen her. Madison calls him “brother dear” and says it is useful to know neighbors because they can sign for packages, lend sugar, or spot condoms in the middle of the night. Fifth asks why, then responds, “Oh.”

plotBeats: Fifth and Madison walk down a busy New York street.
Madison asks Fifth if he knows a woman.
Fifth says he has never seen her before.
Madison says it is good to know one's neighbors, calling him “brother dear.”
Fifth asks why.
Madison lists practical favors neighbors can provide: signing for packages, lending sugar, and spotting condoms in the middle of the night.
Fifth responds, “Oh.”

speaking.goal: Encourage Fifth to value knowing his neighbors and explain the practical benefits.
speaking.name: Madison

speaking.goal: Answer Madison's question and understand why knowing neighbors is useful.

scene_01M4KD5YMZQS71YP589WR5Q689.title: Jetta Gets the Job
scene_01M4KD5YMZQS71YP589WR5Q689.summary: Jetta, searching for work, enters a tattoo shop where Nacho rudely challenges her and questions her claim to be a tattoo artist. She shows her tattooed arm as a portfolio, and the dispute becomes a fight: she knocks Nacho down twice and breaks his nose. Tony recognizes the work as prison-style, apologizes, and offers Jetta a job if she can use the tattoo gun. She accepts. When Nacho threatens to quit, Tony pays him off and ends their working arrangement; Nacho leaves while Jetta and Tony laugh at her parting taunt.

plotBeats: Jetta seeks work at restaurants and shops; a man in a restaurant shakes his head no, and she leaves.
After visiting more restaurants, Jetta enters a tattoo shop.
Nacho tells her the shop works by appointment only; Jetta says she wants work, not a tattoo, and Nacho responds rudely.
Tony arrives, scolds Nacho for his manners, apologizes, and asks Jetta how he can help.
Jetta says she is looking for work. Tony asks if she is an artist, and she shows the detailed tattoos on her arm as her portfolio.
Nacho questions whether Jetta did the work; Jetta snaps back, and their argument escalates despite Tony's attempt to intervene.
Nacho leaps over the counter at Jetta; she sidesteps and strikes him in the ribs, sending him into chairs and onto the floor.
Jetta removes her obstructive white shirt, revealing extensive tattoos. Nacho rises and insists she got lucky and that he will teach her respect.
Nacho attacks with punches; Jetta avoids most of them, then counters with a jab and combination that breaks his nose and floors him.
Tony explains that Jetta's tattoos are prison-style and apologizes. Jetta says she has nothing to apologize for and warns Nacho not to call her a bitch again.
As Jetta starts to leave, Tony asks if she did the tattoo work herself. She confirms she did, and Tony offers her work if she can operate the tattoo gun; Jetta accepts.
Nacho says he will quit if Tony hires Jetta. Tony gives Nacho money and tells him their time working together is over; Nacho leaves.
Jetta calls after Nacho and taunts him; she and Tony laugh as Nacho looks back in disgust.

speaking.emotional_state: increasingly irritated and aggressive, then angry at being dismissed
speaking.goal: Keep control of the shop and reject or intimidate Jetta; then leave when Tony hires her.
speaking.name: Nacho

speaking.emotional_state: initially rude, then appreciative and apologetic, finally amused
speaking.goal: Assess Jetta's tattoo skill and offer her work, while trying to manage Nacho's behavior.
speaking.name: Tony

speaking.emotional_state: determined and self-assured, briefly confrontational, then confident and amused
speaking.goal: Find work, demonstrate her tattooing ability, and secure a job at the shop.
speaking.name: Jetta

scene_01M4KD5YMZVGV56SC2QKJ1NKAC.title: A Dangerous Lead
scene_01M4KD5YMZVGV56SC2QKJ1NKAC.summary: Desmond challenges Marcos over the lack of progress in finding his brother's killer. Marcos says there are no leads, refuses to follow Desmond's dangerous lead, and warns that the person may be too connected to touch. After an argument about Desmond's mention of Cuba, Marcos asks about Fifth. They discuss Fifth's recklessness and his lack of a reason to live, and Desmond explains that he cares about him and sees goodness in him, as he did in his brother. Marcos jokes about the brother's drug dealing but stops when Desmond gives him a serious look. Marcos agrees to do what he can. Desmond leaves the coffee shop, and Marcos watches him from the window.

plotBeats: Desmond and Marcos sit over coffee; Desmond complains that Marcos has found no leads after more than a week.
Marcos says Desmond's brother dealt drugs and may have been killed by a crackhead, and insists that finding him will take time.
Desmond angrily says the killer could be in Cuba; Marcos objects to the Cuba reference, and Desmond says it was only an example.
Desmond asks whether Marcos followed his lead; Marcos says no, explaining that it is dangerous and that the person involved may be too connected to touch.
Marcos tells Desmond to leave him out of it, then asks about Fifth.
Desmond says Fifth is doing well and may settle down while his sister is in town; Marcos recalls Fifth's dangerous behavior, including jumping off a roof, and worries he may die.
Desmond says the world is troubled and that Fifth has not found a reason to live; he says he understands because he has been there.
Marcos asks why Desmond does not let Fifth go; Desmond says he likes him and compares Fifth's good heart with his brother's.
Marcos jokes that Desmond's brother was a good drug dealer; Desmond's serious look stops Marcos's chuckle.
Desmond says his brother and Fifth cared about people and that the world needs more people like them; Marcos agrees to do what he can.
Desmond thanks Marcos, finishes his coffee, grabs his jacket, and leaves; Marcos watches him from the window.

speaking.goal: Get Marcos to find his brother's killer and act on the lead he provided.
speaking.name: Desmond

speaking.emotional_state: defensive, irritated, then concerned and conciliatory
speaking.goal: Explain the lack of progress, avoid following a dangerous lead, and discuss Fifth's welfare with Desmond.
speaking.name: Marcos

scene_01M4KD5YMZ12C574TT40SCMXTV.title: Desmond's Despair and Jetta's Hope
scene_01M4KD5YMZ12C574TT40SCMXTV.summary: Desmond sits alone, drinking and struggling with painful thoughts, then uses music to distract himself. Jetta arrives and tells him she has found work tattooing in Hell's Kitchen. Their joking conversation becomes serious as she asks about his despair and urges him to believe he can still change and find happiness. Desmond says he will try but doubts it is not too late, then begins to mention a past love before stopping Jetta from responding. Fifth and Madison arrive; Madison pushes Desmond to go out for a drink, but he says he is not fit to drive and will not let Fifth drive his car. He starts joking about Fifth's driving as the scene transitions to a flashback.

plotBeats: Desmond sits alone drinking and struggling with painful thoughts, then gets up and puts on music to distract himself.
Jetta enters, sits across from Desmond, and they talk about her new tattoo-shop job and her limited career options as an ex-con.
Desmond goes to the bathroom while they continue bantering, then returns to find Jetta watching him closely.
Jetta asks about Desmond's state of mind; he says he feels changed and hopeless, while she tells him he deserves happiness.
Desmond describes his heartbreak and guilt; Jetta recalls King David and argues that he still has hope and must choose to change.
Desmond says he will try, but doubts it is not too late, and begins to say he once fell in love; he cuts Jetta off and says he never blamed her.
The doorbell rings; Desmond admits Fifth, and Fifth and Madison enter noisily.
Madison invites Desmond out for drinks; Desmond jokes with her and refuses to go immediately because he is not fit to drive.
Desmond says Fifth will not drive his car and jokes about Fifth's driving; the scene cuts into a flashback sequence.

speaking.emotional_state: distressed, self-reproachful, then reflective and resigned
speaking.goal: Pull himself out of his painful thoughts, deflect Jetta's questions, and explain his hopelessness about happiness and the past.
speaking.name: Desmond

speaking.goal: Understand what Desmond is struggling with, reassure him that he can find happiness, and encourage him to turn his life around.
speaking.name: Jetta

speaking.goal: Get Desmond to join her and Fifth for a night out and a drink.

scene_01M4KD5YMZRGZ2EJY5HVSAV44S.title: Fifth's Reckless Drive
scene_01M4KD5YMZRGZ2EJY5HVSAV44S.summary: Fifth drives recklessly with Desmond and two hookers in the car, speeding, running red lights, cutting off another car and hitting a hot dog stand. Desmond protests and tries to take control, eventually hitting Fifth and steering the car into a park bench to avoid a garbage truck. Desmond is bleeding and shaken, while Fifth emerges unhurt and stretches calmly. An elderly bystander questions Fifth, who silently eats pistachios before walking to a tree and tossing nuts to a squirrel.

plotBeats: Fifth drives with Desmond in the passenger seat and two hookers in the back, while Desmond tries to drink a milk shake.
At a red light, men in an adjacent car point and laugh at Fifth; Fifth nods.
When the light turns green, Fifth accelerates sharply and speeds off.
Desmond tells Fifth to slow down.
Fifth speeds past and cuts off the adjacent car, causing it to lose control and hit the island.
Fifth looks in the rear-view mirror, grins and giggles; Desmond insists it is not funny and again tells him to slow down.
Fifth becomes zoned out, drives faster, runs red lights and skids through turns.
Desmond's milk shake flies out of his hand and splashes onto the hookers, who are in the back.
Desmond asks what Fifth is doing and reminds him that he hates car crashes.
Fifth speeds through a busy intersection and hits a hot dog stand.
Desmond says he will not go down with Fifth and reaches for the steering wheel; the hookers scream as Fifth turns up the music with one hand.
Desmond fights for control while Fifth presses harder on the gas and heads toward the back of a garbage truck.
Desmond hits Fifth in the jaw; Fifth releases the wheel, and Desmond turns hard left and pulls the emergency brake, sending the car over the curb into a park bench.
People gather as distant ambulance and police sirens are heard; Fifth forces his door open and gets out.
Desmond and the hookers are shaken, and Desmond is bleeding from the head; Fifth emerges unscathed as the onlookers look perplexed.
Fifth stretches calmly; an elderly bystander approaches and asks if he is okay and what kind of driving that was.
Fifth stares at the man, takes pistachios from his pocket, cracks and eats one while maintaining eye contact.
The bystander backs away; Fifth notices a squirrel by a tree, kneels near it and tosses it nuts.

speaking.goal: Get Fifth to slow down and prevent the car from crashing.
speaking.name: Desmond

speaking.emotional_state: gleeful and zoned out, then calm
speaking.goal: Drive recklessly and enjoy himself, then feed the squirrel.
speaking.name: Fifth

speaking.goal: Check whether Fifth is okay and ask what happened with his driving.
speaking.name: Park Bystander

scene_01M4KD5YMZJDWNB18D0FKCBKZ6.title: Cards and a Quarrel
scene_01M4KD5YMZJDWNB18D0FKCBKZ6.summary: Madison suggests taking a taxi, but Desmond refuses to leave yet. Jetta and Madison joke about going out, then start a card game with Desmond; Fifth joins after Desmond calls him over. The game is close and lively. As they play, Madison asks Jetta about her tattoos and discusses getting one herself, while Desmond reveals the scar on his jaw and dismisses tattoos. A dispute over the card rules erupts when Jetta reaches for the kitty before calling, and the four-way shouting continues as the scene moves into Desmond's car.

plotBeats: Madison suggests taking a taxi, but Desmond refuses to leave until he has waited out the toxins and jokes that nothing new is happening in the city.
Madison says she has numbers to take and hearts to break; Jetta adds that she has ass to shake, and they high five.
Desmond says it is too early for dancing, and Jetta agrees.
Jetta and Madison sit at the table; Jetta takes a deck of cards from a shelf, shuffles, and performs card tricks as Desmond joins them.
Jetta needles Desmond about his card skills and reminds him that she and her partner previously took his shirt in a game; Desmond says he does not remember.
Madison asks how they will get to the party if they send him to Boston; Desmond signals Fifth, who removes himself from the headphones and joins the table.
Desmond tells Fifth the women are talking about sending somebody to Boston; Fifth says he is down.
The card game becomes intense, with animated faces and arguing, while the score remains about even.
Jetta removes her shirt, leaving a tank top, and Madison looks at her tattooed arms and asks about the tattoos and whether they hurt.
Madison says she has thought about getting a tattoo; she and Desmond trade remarks about what kind she might choose.
Madison asks Desmond whether he has considered a tattoo; Desmond shows his jaw scar and says a scar beats a tattoo.
Jetta finishes dealing and asks Fifth for his bid; Fifth and Madison pass, and Desmond bids four low while Jetta takes four no.
Jetta reaches for and looks at the kitty; Desmond objects that she must call uptown or down, and Jetta says she does not have to.
Fifth agrees with Desmond, Madison tells them not to yell at her partner, and the four argue loudly.
The shouting match carries over into Desmond's car.

speaking.goal: Get ready to go out while refusing to leave before he feels recovered, then play cards and enforce his understanding of the rules.
speaking.name: Desmond

speaking.goal: Get the group to the party, play cards, and defend her partner during the argument.

speaking.goal: Play cards, show off her tricks, and enjoy the evening with the group.

scene_01M4KD5YMZFWD5QV9E2GE6ZP4A.title: The Parking Space
scene_01M4KD5YMZFWD5QV9E2GE6ZP4A.summary: In Desmond's car, Jetta and Fifth tell Desmond that he threw his hand in during the card game, but he remains argumentative with Fifth. While they circle the club looking for parking, Madison reminds Desmond that leaving after he sobered up was his idea. He tells her she can walk, prompting Jetta to object and Madison to call him an incurable jackass. When another car reverses into an open space, its Yuppie passenger tells Desmond maybe next time. Desmond pulls a gun and fires twice into the air; the other car speeds away, and everyone inside Desmond's car stares at him in disbelief.

Jetta says Desmond threw his hand in and asks why he is still arguing; Fifth agrees.
Desmond tells Fifth to shut up; Fifth insults Desmond's mother, and Desmond challenges him before Fifth feigns confusion.
They circle around the club while Desmond complains about finding parking.
Madison reminds Desmond that leaving after he sobered up was his idea; Desmond tells her she can get out and walk.
Jetta tells Desmond not to let Madison walk alone; Desmond looks back at Jetta, and she shakes her head in disapproval.
Madison says she knows Desmond does not mean it and calls him an incurable jackass.
Desmond speeds up toward an open parking space as another vehicle reverses dangerously into it; Desmond pulls up beside the car, whose passengers appear to be yuppies.
The Yuppie says they may get the space next time.
Desmond smiles, pulls an automatic from his shoulder holster, sticks his arm out the window, and fires two shots into the air.
The Yuppie exclaims, and the Yuppie car speeds away up the block.
The people inside Desmond's car stare at him in disbelief; Desmond asks, “What?”

scene_01M4KD5YMZY1HYQF5GY5HB9GAR.title: A Ring and a Night Out
scene_01M4KD5YMZY1HYQF5GY5HB9GAR.summary: The quartet arrives at a club, where Jetta takes Fifth to dance while Madison and Desmond sit together. Desmond says he is cutting back on drinking, and Madison apologizes for having left without calling and asks about his troubles. She notices his engagement ring on a chain, and he explains the lost relationship behind it and recounts a drunken shooting that killed a woman; he says the ring later gave him hope. Madison encourages him to have hope and let others help, but Desmond doubts that things will improve. Jetta and Fifth dance as women gather around them. Ray approaches Madison and offers to pay; Desmond initially tells him to leave, then greets and introduces him as his friend. Ray and Madison exchange flirtatious courtesies. Madison jokes with Desmond about his friends and watches her brother dance. After Madison drinks, the group gathers in the VIP booth, where they laugh, dance, shout, and drink with Ray and an attractive young woman.

plotBeats: The quartet enters a club with a mature, dressed-up crowd; Jetta says she likes it, grabs Fifth, and takes him to the dance floor.
Madison asks Desmond to buy her a drink; they sit in a booth, receive drinks, and Desmond tips the cocktail waitress.
Madison asks what Desmond is drinking; he says cranberry juice, explains he is cutting back, and trades jokes with her.
Madison asks if Desmond is alright and apologizes for leaving without calling; Desmond says he has been in a bad place but regards them as family.
Madison invites Desmond to talk; she grabs the chain and engagement ring under his shirt, and he explains that he keeps it as a reminder of what might have been.
Desmond recounts his serious relationship after Madison left, the proposal that was delayed, and the woman's return from abroad pregnant and married.

Desmond describes years of drinking and despair, then recounts a flashback in which, drunk, he mistakes his service revolver for a drink, fires, and kills a woman; he says he was suspended and that the ring later gave him hope.
Madison tells Desmond things can improve and urges him to let people help; Desmond doubts that life will get better for him.
On the dance floor, Jetta and Fifth dance as women gather around Fifth; Jetta pushes away a woman who tries to cut in.
Desmond and Madison joke about getting drunk, and Madison downs her drink.
Ray approaches, compliments Madison, and offers to pay for the drinks; Madison invites him to join them, while Desmond tells him to leave.
Ray challenges Desmond, then Desmond and Ray shake hands and hug; Desmond introduces Ray to his sister Madison.
Ray compliments Madison, kisses her hand, and leaves, saying he may join them later.
Madison teases Desmond about his friends and notices her brother break-dancing; Desmond says Fifth is not a keeper.
Desmond calls for the bartender; after some time, Desmond and Madison join Fifth and Jetta in the VIP booth, where the group laughs, dances, shouts, and drinks with Ray and an attractive young woman.

speaking.name: Madison

scene_01M4KD5YMZ6ZVTZF1NCW0F2JAF.title: Sleep After the Club
scene_01M4KD5YMZ6ZVTZF1NCW0F2JAF.summary: In Desmond's apartment, sunlight streams through the open window in his bedroom as Desmond sleeps comfortably with the young girl who was Ray's escort the previous night. On the couch, Jetta tosses and turns while holding a furry stuffed dog.

plotBeats: Sunlight beams through the open window in Desmond's bedroom.
Desmond sleeps comfortably while holding the young girl who was Ray's escort the previous night.
Jetta tosses and turns on the couch, clutching a stuffed dog.

scene_01M4KD5YMZCCW36E24TK4SQH1Z.title: Interrupted Bath
scene_01M4KD5YMZCCW36E24TK4SQH1Z.summary: In Fifth's loft, Madi sleeps held by Ray while Fifth takes a bath with a small television balanced precariously on the tub. Water spills as Fifth shifts around, and pounding from the downstairs neighbor interrupts him. Fifth leaps out, wraps a towel around himself, grabs a Cowboy T-shirt, and rushes out; the television then falls into the tub and the outlet explodes.

plotBeats: Madi sleeps while held by Ray in Fifth's loft, beneath a satin sheet as sunlight fills the room.
A faint morning news broadcast comes from a small television balanced on the edge of a bathtub filled with water, where Fifth sits wide-eyed.
Fifth shifts in the tub, spilling water over its edge as the television teeters close to falling in; he appears oblivious to the danger.
Loud pounding from the downstairs neighbor disrupts Fifth's bath, finally breaking the morning's peacefulness.
Fifth leaps out of the tub, wraps a towel around his waist, grabs a Cowboy T-shirt from the floor, and rushes out of the bathroom.
After Fifth leaves, the television falls into the tub and the wall outlet explodes.

speaking.name: Fifth

scene_01M4KD5YMZA1XFMQC1XEPM6S54.title: The Upstairs Neighbor
scene_01M4KD5YMZA1XFMQC1XEPM6S54.summary: Fifth, wearing only a towel and a wet T-shirt, knocks on apartment F's door and identifies himself as Sidney's upstairs neighbor. Sidney opens the door, accuses him of leaking water onto her prints, and pulls him inside by his shirt, taking him to the bathroom. Sidney accuses Fifth of leaking water onto her prints and tells him to come inside.

scene_01M4KD5YMZ5YQM7XZZ60F3CP9C.title: A Promise and a Memory
scene_01M4KD5YMZ5YQM7XZZ60F3CP9C.summary: Desmond sees Ray's Girl out after they kiss, then gets cereal while Jetta emerges and teases him about the previous night. They discuss Ray's Girl, and Desmond says he wants Marcos to help find Jetta's son, though he will postpone finding Pop's killer. When Desmond says he would kill the killer, Jetta urges him to let the courts handle it, but he rejects her advice and says the system is a joke. Desmond explains that his childhood experience of being beaten and ignored inspired him to help others. Jetta says she misses her son and cannot picture him; Desmond hugs her and promises they will find him.

plotBeats: Desmond leaves his bedroom in boxers with Ray's Girl, kisses her, and sees her out after she asks him to call.
Desmond starts preparing cereal as Jetta emerges from beneath the sheets and blankets and asks what day it is.
Jetta and Desmond trade teasing remarks about their nights; Jetta throws a stuffed dog at Desmond, hitting him and spilling cereal.
Jetta asks how Desmond ended up with Ray's Girl; he says Madi brought them together, and they discuss Ray and Desmond's view that he is trouble.
Desmond says he wants Jetta to meet Marcos, a former police colleague now working as a private investigator, and says he will ask him to help find her son.
Jetta asks whether Marcos can help find both her son and Pop's killer; Desmond says finding her son will be hard and expensive, so the search for Pop's killer must wait.
Jetta asks what Desmond will do if he finds the killer; he says he will kill him, and she urges him to let the courts decide.
Desmond rejects the courts and Jetta observes that he has changed; Desmond shifts the subject to finding her son, and she thanks him for helping.
Desmond says he wants to help Jetta; she says he has always loved helping people, and he laughs that it was not always so.
Desmond recounts how, as a child, he was beaten on his walk home and ignored by passersby, prompting his resolve to help children he sees in trouble.
Jetta says the story is sad; Desmond says it led him to help people and offers to call Marcos.
Jetta says she misses her son and cannot picture what he looks like now; Desmond hugs her and promises they will find him.

speaking.emotional_state: casual and amused, later defensive about revenge and reflective when recounting his childhood; reassuring at the end
speaking.goal: Arrange for Marcos to help locate Jetta's son while postponing the search for Pop's killer, and reassure Jetta.
speaking.name: Desmond

speaking.emotional_state: playful and teasing, then concerned and earnest, ultimately vulnerable about missing her son
speaking.goal: Learn what Desmond intends to do, urge him away from killing, and seek help finding her son.
speaking.name: Jetta

speaking.goal: Tell Desmond she enjoyed their time and ask him to call her.

scene_01M4KD5YMZ0VM7V5YZAKYP4CZD.title: A Search for Marlon

She explains that she cut off contact with her son while in prison, that her marriage cannot return to what it was, and that she wants her son to know his mother. Marcos says finding the family will require a bribe and privately quotes Desmond five thousand dollars for the effort. Marcos leaves after promising to be in touch, while Jetta and Desmond remain seated listening to the music and people-watching.

Desmond explains his behavior, and they joke about his use of paid sex.

Marcos privately identifies Jetta as the woman from the Gathers murder, but Desmond signals him not to mention it.
Jetta hears Marcos, admits her identity, says she served her time, and challenges him; Marcos says he has no argument with her.
Marcos asks about Jetta's son; Jetta explains that the boy's father moved him after the trial and that she asked her husband not to contact her while she was in prison.
Jetta says she could not cope with letters and visits, does not expect to resume her marriage, and wants her son to know his mother; she says Marlon will turn eight this year.

Marcos wishes Jetta well and leaves into the crowd; Jetta and Desmond sit and watch people as the music continues.

Steven says someone will meet Jetta at JFK at 1 PM that day and that this is her only chance before they move again; Jetta agrees to go and asks about her son.
Steven puts Marlon on the phone. Jetta and Marlon greet one another, and Marlon asks why Jetta is crying.
Jetta says she is happy to hear him and has missed him; Marlon says he misses her and asks if she is coming to see him and daddy.
Jetta promises she will come and tells Marlon she loves him; they say they love each other and end their call.
Steven returns to the phone; Jetta thanks him and says she will see him soon, and Steven wishes her a safe trip.
Jetta puts down the phone, cries, and walks to the window to look out at the morning sky.

scene_01M4KD5YMZ2YP3MKQDE57ND1Q6.title: Fifth's Family Secrets
scene_01M4KD5YMZ2YP3MKQDE57ND1Q6.summary: In bed with Sidney, Fifth fondly remembers his mother and reflects on how he lived for her after a childhood suicide attempt, and how he lost the will after her death. When he says his father ran away, Sidney recognizes that he is lying; Fifth explains that his mother never told him what happened and that Madi said his father had died. They discuss how Sidney read the lie, and Fifth says he is in love with her. He gets up and they make plans: Sidney wants to photograph him, and Fifth agrees to let her come along to something he needs to do, with Sidney offering to drive.

plotBeats: Sidney and Fifth lie in bed talking, with Sidney's head on Fifth's chest; Fifth recalls his mother's unusual Sunday-school alternative of taking him and Madi shopping.
Fifth says he misses his mother and wishes she could meet Sidney; they joke about whether Sidney would have impressed her.
Fifth reflects on having hated the world and wanting to leave, and wonders whether there is a better place after death; he says his mother's material comforts did not necessarily make her happy.
Fifth tells Sidney that a childhood suicide attempt ended when he saw how much it hurt his mother, and that he lived for her; after losing her, he lost the will.
Sidney asks about his father. Fifth says his father ran away and started another family, but Sidney says she knows he is lying.
Fifth explains that his mother never told him what happened and that Madi told him his father died and was unhappy; he says he does not remember a funeral.
Sidney explains how she detected the lie, and Fifth remarks that he would find her insight unsettling if he were not in love with her.
Fifth gets out of bed and looks out the window, then asks about their plans for the day.
Sidney proposes taking photos of Fifth; he jokes about modelling, asks about nudity, and agrees, saying he has something to do first.
Sidney asks to come along, and Fifth agrees; they decide to take the car, but Fifth does not feel like driving, so Sidney offers to drive despite having no license.

speaking.emotional_state: warm and curious, then concerned and perceptive
speaking.goal: Connect with Fifth, ask about his mother and father, and understand what he is comfortable sharing.
speaking.name: Sidney

speaking.emotional_state: affectionate and nostalgic, then somber and vulnerable, ending playful
speaking.goal: Share memories and feelings about his family with Sidney, then make plans for the day.
speaking.name: Fifth

scene_01M4KD5YMZDV6ZXPG8VZ67J79E.title: A Proposal and a Collision
scene_01M4KD5YMZDV6ZXPG8VZ67J79E.summary: Sidney and Fifth enjoy a sunny shopping outing before Fifth secretly visits Peacle's Jewelry. The Peacles welcome him and give him a ring his mother had chosen and paid for; Fifth takes it to propose to Sidney. Back in the car he asks her three playful questions, ending with a marriage proposal, and Sidney joyfully accepts. The ring fits perfectly, and they set out to celebrate and tell Madi and Des. Distracted by admiring the ring, Sidney drives through a red light and their car is struck on the passenger side by a speeding moving truck.

plotBeats: Sidney drives Fifth on a sunny day as they sing, look at clouds, and collect shopping bags in the back seat.
Fifth asks Sidney to stop so he can get something as a surprise; he slips away while she tries to watch him.
Fifth visits Peacle's Jewelry, where Mrs. Peacle welcomes him and calls Mr. Peacle from the back.
The Peacles greet Fifth and speak fondly of his late mother; Mr. Peacle guesses Fifth has met someone and takes him to the back room.

Mr. Peacle retrieves a ring his wife says Fifth's mother chose and paid for; Fifth accepts it and tips Mr. Peacle with money from Des's envelope.

scene_01M4KD5YMZFD1D9RT3ASR6BZQ0.title: Flowers at Madi's Bed
scene_01M4KD5YMZFD1D9RT3ASR6BZQ0.summary: Desmond experiences a sharp chest pain while carrying flowers to Madi's hospital room and drops the vase. A nurse helps him gather the flowers and tells him to sit down. He brings the flowers to sleeping Madi and sits by her bed, then answers Jetta's call. She says she must leave that day to see Marlon and wishes she could stay with Madi. Desmond encourages her to go, offers to drive her, and says he will ask Fifth to come to the hospital in case Madi wakes. After ending the call, Desmond tells Madi he needs her and urges her to recover, then kisses her on the head on Jetta's behalf.

plotBeats: Desmond walks toward Madi's hospital room carrying flowers when a sharp pain in his chest makes him drop the vase, which breaks.
Desmond gathers the flowers, and a nurse helps him and asks if he is alright; he describes the chest pain, and she tells him to sit while she takes care of it.
Desmond carries the flowers into Madi's room, where she is sleeping, places them in a container, and sits by her bed.
His cell phone rings and startles him; he hesitates before answering Jetta's call.
Jetta asks where he is and how Madi is; Desmond says he is at the hospital, that the problem is under control, and that Madi is in bad shape after surgery.
Jetta tells Desmond she has heard from Marlon and must leave that day to meet someone at JFK; she says she wishes she could stay with Madi.
Desmond encourages Jetta to go see her son after waiting five years and offers to drive her; he says he will call Fifth to come sit with Madi in case she wakes.
Jetta says she will pack and take a cab, and Desmond insists he wants to see her before she leaves; they agree he will come in 20 minutes.
Jetta asks Desmond to kiss Madi for her and says she will pray for her; Desmond agrees.
Desmond puts away the phone, speaks to Madi about her strength, apologizes, says she is his sister and friend and that he needs her, and urges her to get better.
Desmond kisses Madison on the head and tells her the kiss is from Jetta.

speaking.emotional_state: in pain and worried, later affectionate and distressed
speaking.goal: Get to Madi's room, remain with her, and reassure her; coordinate with Jetta about seeing Marlon.
speaking.name: Desmond

speaking.emotional_state: concerned and grateful, then reluctant to leave Madi but determined to see her son

scene_01M4KD5YMZ1RE80BXE3X9AXXT3.title: Desmond's Worry on the Drive
scene_01M4KD5YMZ1RE80BXE3X9AXXT3.summary: Desmond leaves Fifth a message from the hospital parking lot that Madi is hospitalized and he is taking Jetta to JFK. While driving with Jetta, he admits he is not okay and blames himself for Madi's injury. He explains that she set up Ray Oaklin to learn that Ray killed Pop, and Jetta asks if Desmond killed him. Jetta tells Desmond Madi wanted to help and urges him not to blame himself. They discuss Fifth's likely reaction to Madi being hospitalized; Desmond says she had helped keep Fifth stable and that he may need to put Marcos back on him. He explains that Marcos was hired by Fifth's firm to stop Fifth from killing himself, and that the firm could face a large payout because everything is in Madi's name. Desmond says he will call Marcos when they reach the airport, and admits he does not know whether he will be alright.

scene_01M4KD5YMZZ0SYRMCA56B5BHQP.title: A Farewell and a Ring
scene_01M4KD5YMZZ0SYRMCA56B5BHQP.summary: At the airport terminal, Jetta prepares to board a plane as a man in a black suit waits for her. She says goodbye to Desmond, thanking him for everything he has done. Desmond says he wants to see her happy, and Jetta replies that she is happy when she is with him. They kiss; Jetta reaches into Desmond's shirt and holds the ring, telling him she will return for it if he makes the right choice. After they look into each other's eyes, Jetta walks away, and Desmond watches her until she is gone, with a solitary tear on his face.
